newsitem.title: UK: Clarke leaves dividend tax credits untouched.
newsitem.headline: Clarke leaves dividend tax credits untouched.

text.p: Pension funds and fund management companies breathed a collective sigh of relief after British Chancellor Kenneth Clarke's budget speech on Tuesday when he left the rate of tax credits on dividends unchanged.
Many tax experts and analysts had thought that Clarke might cut the tax credit to 15 percent from 20 percent which would have raised around 1.0 billion stg per year.
"It's a big relief for the many institutions who expected to be raided," said one tax expert at a major accountancy firm.

But some analysts had said before the budget that such a move would have acted against the Government's long-term objective of encouraging increased private savings provision and might have been a burden on the corporate sector.
This would have happened if institutional shareholders had put pressure on companies to compensate by increasing gross dividend payouts.

Roger Bootle, group chief economist at HSBC Markets, had also warned that the Chancellor might want to avoid newspaper headlines along the lines of "Mr Clarke raids your pension - to give you an income tax cut."
